transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-19
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood), Laura Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Morales (Redwood), Ava Thompson (SummitPay), Marcus Lee (SummitPay Sec Arch), Priya Raman (SummitPay PM)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Laura, our SE, and Diego from solutions. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Ava: Good, thanks. Ready to see the retention controls — we've been trying to lock down logging and PII across our payment flows.
[00:12] Samir: Great. Quick agenda: 1) short discovery on your current stack and regulatory needs, 2) console + API demo of retention and redaction, 3) Q&A and next steps.
[00:22] Marcus: Quick note — we're PCI-adjacent, not storing card PANs in cleartext anywhere; we want to make sure Redwood won't persist payment identifiers and that we can control retention at request-level.
[00:32] Laura: Absolutely. We'll show both the Console toggles and the API flags — request-level opt-out and auto-redaction in our pipeline.
[00:38] Priya: Also curious about encryption at rest, KMS integration, and audit trails.
[00:42] Laura: Yep. We'll cover KMS, HSM possibilities, and where audit logs are surfaced.

[00:55] --- Demo starts ---
[01:05] Laura: Okay, switching to the Redwood Console. (screen share) Up top you can see our model routes. I'm going to click into the "Data Controls" tab — you can see default org-level retention is 90 days, but we support per-route overrides.
[01:20] Laura: Here, for the payments route we can flip "Store requests" to off — that setting disables request body storage for that route. It also surfaces a per-request override if you use the API header: x-redwood-store: false.
[01:36] Ava: So the header wins over console? If we set store=false in the API it will not store that single request?
[01:41] Laura: Right. Priority order is: request-level header -> route-level setting -> org default. There is also an "auto-redact" toggle which applies pattern-based redaction for common PII like emails, PAN-like numbers, and SSNs.
[01:55] Marcus: How robust are those patterns? False positives are a concern for our logs.
[01:59] Laura: We use a combination of regex-based detectors and optional integration with our PII classifier — the model-based detector reduces FP, but we always surface a live preview in the console so you can validate. You can add custom regexes for your tokens too.
[02:15] Priya: Does auto-redact mutate the request before storing, or is it only applied to the stored copy?
[02:20] Laura: It's applied prior to persistence — the stored copy will be redacted. Optionally you can enable "store original encrypted" for compliance, which encrypts the original payload with a customer KMS key and restricts access via RBAC and audit logs.
[02:33] Marcus: Ok that's good. For e-discovery we might need the ability to decrypt under legal request — how does access work?
[02:38] Laura: Decryption requires a KMS permission tied to the customer's key and RBAC role in the console. All decrypt operations are logged to the audit trail and show up in our immutable audit logs.

[03:00] Samir: Quick callout — you can also use our API flag to route sensitive requests to a Dedicated pool or to a Private deployment if you need network isolation. That helps with regulatory controls and reduces the need to use encrypted originals at rest.
[03:12] Marcus: We're evaluating Dedicated versus Private — what's the difference from a data handling perspective?
[03:16] Diego: Dedicated gives you isolated GPU capacity and tenancy, but control plane is still in Redwood; Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you a customer-managed control plane and networking. In Private you own the KMS and can enforce strict egress rules.
[03:29] Ava: Does the Private package support our HSM via AWS CloudHSM / external HSM?
[03:33] Laura: Yes, we integrate with AWS KMS and CloudHSM, and for air-gapped setups we support HSM appliances via standard PKCS#11 integrations.

[03:50] [04:05] Laura: Back to the Console — here is the audit log view. You can filter by event type: decryption events, retention toggles changed, API flag usage, and who made changes. Logs are exportable and streamable to your SIEM.
[04:20] Marcus: Is the audit log tamper-evident?
[04:24] Laura: We support append-only logs with signed entries and an option to stream to your external logging bucket for archival.

[04:40] [05:10] Ava: Can you show the API payload that disables storage?
[05:15] Laura: Sure — example: POST /v1/generate with header x-redwood-store: false and header x-redwood-mask: strict. We also have a per-tenant header to set KMS key id: x-redwood-kms-key: arn:aws:kms:...
[05:32] Samir: Note that setting x-redwood-store:false means we will not persist the request body; however, ephemeral metadata like request timestamps and token counts may still be retained for billing unless you purchase a privacy add-on.
[05:46] Marcus: Wait, token counts? For billing we need to reconcile costs without sending us data. Can you export usage without request-level detail?
[05:52] Laura: Yes — we have aggregated billing reports by route and time window that show token totals, costs, and latency percentiles. Those reports can be generated without storing individual requests.

[06:10] [06:25] Priya: About PII redaction — if the model generates a suggestion that contains a masked value, do we get the masked output or the original in the response?
[06:33] Laura: The API response to your application will be the generated content. Redaction is applied to stored records; runtime responses are not mutated by the storage redaction. If you want runtime filtering you can enable pre- and post-processing hooks in the route that filter outputs before forwarding to your app.

[06:55] [07:10] Marcus: Compliance wise, we need encryption at rest with CMAK — customer-managed keys and rotation. Is key rotation supported?
[07:16] Laura: Yes, KMS rotation is supported; for customer-managed keys you control rotation policy. For Private deployments, rotation is fully in your hands. We document key rotation steps and have automation helpers.

[07:40] [08:05] Samir: I also want to highlight our "redaction policies" feature in Optimize — you can run a batch of historical logs through the redaction engine in a sandbox, see what would be redacted, and tune rules before enabling in production.
[08:20] Ava: That sandbox sounds useful — can we run it on our sample dataset?
[08:24] Laura: Yes, we can import CSV or streamed logs. For POC we'll run your sample traffic through and show false positive/negative rates.

[08:40] [09:05] Priya: For legal holds, we sometimes need to retain data beyond org retention for a subset of requests. Is there a way to pin requests?
[09:12] Laura: We have a "pin" API that marks a request as preserved; pinning is allowed only if org policy permits it and will store the encrypted original. Pins are visible in the console under Legal Holds.
[09:24] Marcus: Are pins only for originals, or can you pin redacted copies?
[09:28] Laura: You can pin either; default is to pin the encrypted original. If you need only the redacted copy retained, you can choose that when pinning.

[09:50] [10:10] Ava: How does SSO/SAML integrate for RBAC? We have strict role separation between platform and security teams.
[10:16] Laura: We support SAML and SCIM provisioning. Roles map to console roles and API scopes. Decryption rights and KMS key use are tied to roles.

[10:40] [11:05] Marcus: Let's talk retention periods — what's the minimum? Some regs demand deletion within 30 days.
[11:12] Laura: You can set retention down to zero — immediate discard — though note audit/usage traces may remain as aggregates. For stricter needs we recommend Private where you control every store.
[11:24] Priya: Would zero retention affect debugging and model performance analysis?
[11:28] Laura: It reduces our ability to debug edge cases. Our suggested pattern is to use short retention for production and enable longer retention in a dedicated debug route or a canary with obfuscated data.

[11:45] [12:10] Samir: Quick product note: we also surface a "redaction score" in the Optimize tab — it highlights how likely a request contains PII by model inference and flags high-risk flows for you.
[12:24] Ava: How accurate is that? We don't want a flood of false positives.
[12:28] Laura: We tune the model with your sample corpus during POC to reduce FP. The score is just advisory and you can tune thresholds per-route.

[12:55] [13:20] Diego: Another config: automated expirations can be set per-tenant with legal hold overrides. We also support streaming encrypted originals to your archival S3 for long-term storage, which you control access to.
[13:40] Marcus: For archived originals, do you provide a separate index or pointer table? We want to avoid storing metadata that could be PII.
[13:46] Laura: You can choose the level of metadata we retain for archives. Minimal index records will only have non-identifying pointers and timestamps; full indexing is optional.

[14:10] [14:40] Priya: Can we disable logging of prompt text for internal dev routes but keep token counts?
[14:48] Laura: Yes — toggles allow you to log only token counts and latency without storing any textual content. This is common for cost-monitoring while preserving privacy.

[15:05] [15:40] Samir: We'll pause for any security-specific questions. Marcus?
[15:45] Marcus: Two things: 1) do you have a written attestation for data residency and 2) how do you handle subpoenas?
[15:52] Samir: We have a data residency doc — we can pin deployments to region and for subpoenas we follow your legal process: we notify the customer and only release data per legal obligations unless a court order prohibits notice. We'll include the legal process doc in the package.

[16:20] [16:40] Laura: Quick demo of the API: showing a sample request with x-redwood-store:false and x-redwood-mask:strict, and you'll see in the audit that the request was processed but body not stored. (shows audit log entry) The event says "request processed - storage:false" and has no persisted body link.
[17:00] Ava: Nice. Can we get that audit log stream into Splunk?
[17:04] Laura: Yes — we support log forwarding via HTTPS/Syslog and also a Kafka sink for high-volume streaming.

[17:25] [17:50] Priya: For the POC we'll want to run a benchmark for latency and cost with storage disabled vs enabled — any deviations expected?
[17:58] Laura: Minimal. The extra latency for redaction is usually sub-10ms when using regex detectors; model-based PII detection may add 10-30ms depending on model variant. Storage I/O cost is separate — disabling storage removes write cost and slightly reduces tail latency. We'll capture these in the POC.

[18:25] [18:50] Diego: Also note that for large batch workloads, our batcher behaves differently when storage is disabled — we can still batch inferencing but we'll avoid writing intermediate cache to persistent store. Impact on throughput is negligible.

[19:10] [19:35] Marcus: On the legal hold pins, can we export pinned items list as a CSV for legal team?
[19:40] Laura: Yes — exportable with configurable columns; again you can opt to exclude redacted content in the export.

[20:00] [20:20] Priya: About the Optimize feature you mentioned — redaction sandbox — do you have metric outputs e.g., precision/recall?
[20:27] Laura: The sandbox runs a scan and reports precision/recall estimates and highlights rare patterns for manual review. We also output the expected FP rate at the chosen threshold so you can tune.

[20:50] [21:10] Samir: Switching to a couple of customer scenarios — Ava, you said you're PCI-adjacent; what's your biggest blocker to moving data to a managed inference platform?
[21:18] Ava: Primarily control over raw request storage and proof of key custody. Also how quickly we can turn off storage across all routes and guarantee deletion.
[21:28] Samir: Understood. For proof, we'll provide KMS integration docs and for deletion we provide deletion log entries with signed timestamps.

[21:45] [22:05] Marcus: About signed timestamps — are those cryptographically verifiable?
[22:10] Laura: Yes — we sign audit entries with our key and we can include hash chains if you need stronger tamper-evidence.

[22:30] [22:55] Priya: If we route to a Dedicated pool, can we still use the store=false header?
[22:59] Laura: Yes, store flags operate at request level across Hosted and Dedicated. For Dedicated we also offer private retention policies per pool.

[23:25] [23:50] Ava: For the POC we'll want to test both Hosted with store=false and Dedicated with private retention. Can you provision a small Dedicated pool for the week?
[23:58] Samir: We can. For a short POC we typically spin up a small reserved capacity with a temporary commit. We'll include cost estimates.

[24:20] [24:45] Marcus: One more Q on SSO: how granular are session tokens? Can we restrict decrypt operations to certain IP ranges?
[24:52] Laura: Yes — session policies can include IP allow lists and time windows. Decrypt operations are further gated by RBAC and require the KMS permission.

[25:10] [25:30] Priya: Ok, any performance trade-offs for enabling encryption of originals with customer KMS?
[25:36] Diego: The encryption step adds minimal CPU time; larger impact is on key retrieval latency for cold keys. We recommend caching key metadata and using regional KMS endpoints to minimize latency.

[25:55] [26:20] Samir: We'll wrap up with a recap of next steps. To confirm: Samir sends security pack and SOC2 docs; Laura shares recording and screenshots; team schedules POC April 5-9; Marcus provides sample traffic and PII schema.
[26:38] Ava: Sounds good. One ask: include example policy templates for redaction rules so our compliance team can review.
[26:46] Laura: We'll add a template in the share.

[26:55] [27:10] Marcus: Thanks the demo was useful. Quick last ask — can you show the retention policy JSON we can apply via API?
[27:16] Laura: Sure — example payload: POST /v1/admin/policies { "route": "payments", "retention_days": 30, "store": false, "auto_redact": "strict" } — (note: transcripter may garble quotes) — you can push via our admin API or set via Console.
[27:40] Priya: Perfect.

[27:55] [28:20] Samir: Any final questions?
[28:24] Ava: No, thank you. We'll regroup internally and send details to Marcus and Priya.
[28:30] Samir: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and a POC proposal.
[28:40] --- meeting end (recording stops) ---
